text:
jules_kim: prod alert: customer acme-sydney started getting 429s across multiple endpoints ~2026-03-17T10:02Z. Support dashboard shows RPM and TPM close to quota. Can we triage?
support-bot: Alert: rate_limit_exceeded for tenant=acme-sydney, region=ap-southeast-2, code=429, sample_ts=2026-03-17T10:02:12Z
alex_wu: do we have the response headers? X-RateLimit stuff or our internal throttling header?
jules_kim: pasted from customer curl response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-Redwood-Limit-RPM: 600
X-Redwood-Remaining-RPM: 0
X-Redwood-Limit-TPM: 12000
X-Redwood-Remaining-TPM: 4
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","reason":"rpm_exceeded"}
```
maria_gonzalez: Remaining-RPM=0 while Remaining-TPM still >0 is a classic minute-boundary/rollover spike. Ask whether client is fanouting webhooks or doing short polling at the top of the minute.
jules_kim: customer says they have ~50 workers that retry failed webhooks every 5s with no jitter. Sharing nginx upstream logs: 
```
2026-03-17T10:01:58Z POST /v1/gen 200 120ms
2026-03-17T10:02:00Z POST /v1/gen 429 3ms
2026-03-17T10:02:00Z POST /v1/gen 429 2ms
2026-03-17T10:02:00Z POST /v1/gen 429 1ms
2026-03-17T10:02:01Z POST /v1/gen 429 2ms
```
sanjay_rao: yep that's a retry-hotloop hitting the per-minute bucket. Mitigations: client-side exponential backoff + random jitter, reduce fanout, batch requests where possible. On our side: we can enable short quota bump and enable burst smoothing on their tenant to smooth minute spikes.
carmen_li: if we recommend a quota bump, what's the safe increment and timeframe? customer is asking for immediate relief.
alex_wu: propose temp increase RPM 600->1200 for 24h while they deploy fixes. Also enable tenant-level burst_smoothing (token refill smoothing) so minute bursts are spread across window. We should also provide guidance: expose X-Redwood-Reset and full headers so client can align backoff.
maria_gonzalez: runbook steps (short): 1) Approve 24h RPM bump to 1200 (ops ticket). 2) Turn on burst_smoothing for tenant. 3) Ask client to stop tight retry loops, implement exp. backoff with jitter (recommend base=1s, cap=60s, jitter=full). 4) Collect traces using trace-id header and check post-deploy.
jules_kim: requested quota bump via billing-admin, created ticket #BILL-4721. Notified customer to implement jitter and reduced retry frequency.
sanjay_rao: also suggest short-term routing: pin them to dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbor effect if they expect sustained increase. That requires sales sign-off but can be quick for enterprise customers.
carmen_li: customer asks for sample backoff snippet — sending quick JS example: 
```js
// simple exp backoff with jitter
async function retry(fn, attempts=6) {
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++) {
    try { return await fn(); } catch(e) {
      const base = Math.min(1000 * 2**i, 60000);
      const wait = Math.floor(Math.random()*base);
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, wait));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries');
}
```
alex_wu: good. also tell them to honor Retry-After and X-Redwood-Remaining headers. We'll add a short note to the SDK docs.
maria_gonzalez: I'll follow up with a postmortem template to capture root cause and final remediation. For now keep this thread updated — once quota bump confirmed we'll mark resolved. :white_check_mark:
jules_kim: quota bump approved and applied at 2026-03-17T10:12Z. Customer reports error rate dropped after they deployed jitter. Will monitor for 24h and then revert if stable. Thanks team :thumbsup:
